insights.topic: Deterministic purchase signal vs. probabilistic targeting
insights.insight: At 9,052 verified receipts and $684,959.93 in confirmed GMV, every signal here is a cryptographically proven transaction — not an inferred intent. The ad industry pays $5+ CPM to guess someone might buy; this protocol confirms they did.

insights.topic: Weekly run rate crossing $100K and accelerating
insights.insight: The 7-day GMV window went from $53K on April 1 to a $111.8K peak on April 7 — more than doubling in one week. Post-midnight rollbacks are rolling-window artifacts; cumulative GMV has risen monotonically across every observed cycle.

Retail/department stores leads all categories in GMV ($69,275 over 14 days) at ~$162 per receipt, while Amazon ranks second by receipt count in the trailing window — confirming e-commerce transactions are a meaningful and growing share of the verified signal pool.

insights.topic: Geographic diffusion reaching simultaneous metro and rural coverage
insights.insight: The April 7 heartbeat added 14 CBSAs in a single cycle, including NYC, LA, Philadelphia, Boston, and Seattle alongside CA, NY, PA, and WI non-metro areas — meaning verified purchase signals are no longer concentrated in a single market tier.

insights.topic: Secondary market and creator economy receipts entering the mix
insights.insight: Depop (peer-to-peer resale) and digital commerce vendors including Stripe, Paddle, Gumroad, and Suno now appear in the DKIM vendor set — signaling the protocol is capturing commerce beyond physical retail into resale and the creator economy.

insights.topic: Velocity trend: successive peaks rising above 1.0x floor
insights.insight: Token velocity hit a record 1.232x on April 7, with each successive velocity peak higher than the last since the 1.0x crossover on April 2. The floor has risen — even recovery cycles after rollbacks are holding above 1.0x, indicating sustained throughput expansion rather than episodic spikes.
